title: How to Do the Bird Dog for Beginners (Back & Core Exercise at Home)
intro: The bird dog is a crawling-position exercise where you lift the opposite arm and leg. It trains back and core stability in a slow, controlled way, and suits all levels.
muscles: Lower back muscles (erector spinae), glutes, deep core muscles and shoulder stabiliser muscles. It also trains coordination and balance.
steps: Get on all fours: hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Tighten your tummy slightly, keep your back flat like a table.
Straighten your right arm forward and left leg back at the same time.
Hold 2-3 seconds without letting your hips twist.
Lower slowly, then switch to left arm and right leg.
mistakes: Lifting the leg too high until the back arches. Hip level is enough.
Hips tilting to one side. Imagine a cup of water sitting on your lower back.
Going too fast. Move slowly and control every rep.
easier: Lift only the arm first, then only the leg. Once you're stable, combine arm and leg.
harder: Hold 5 seconds each rep, or bring elbow and knee together under your body before straightening again.
dose: Beginner: 2-3 sets x 6-8 reps each side, hold 2-3 seconds. Can do 3-5 times a week, also good as a warm-up.
safety: Stop if your back pain gets worse or pain spreads down to your leg. If you have chronic back pain, a disc problem (slipped disc) or wrist pain, see a doctor or physiotherapist first.

faq.q: Is the bird dog suitable for people who often have back pain?
faq.a: Many physiotherapists use the bird dog because it's gentle on the spine. But every case is different. If you have back pain, get clearance from your doctor or physio first and stop if the pain gets worse.

faq.q: My body keeps wobbling, is that normal?
faq.a: Normal for beginners. Slow down, tighten your tummy and make the movement smaller. Over time your body will be more stable.

faq.q: My wrists hurt when I'm on all fours, what do I do?
faq.a: Spread your fingers wide and press your whole palm down. You can also put a folded towel under your palms, or support yourself on your fists.
